lifecycle.ready_for_validation_summary: At product commit b8f827a1b6023e17fc3edbcabbc197a1ba9a1331, a normal Windows launch with WGPU_BACKEND absent reached a responsive live Handshake window after the required DX12 feature anchor. External Win32 PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT) captured the exact non-foreground live HWND to a 1500x1300 PNG, which was opened and inspected. The 66 ms capture bracket preserved foreground, active HWND, focused HWND, mouse-capture HWND, cursor coordinates, and both target Z-order neighbours. The final headless test passed 1/1 and its independently re-read JSON contains status=deferred and marker=screenshot_deferred_headless_gpu. Operator waiver WAIVE_MT126_SCOPE:Cargo.toml,Cargo.lock authorizes the two required manifest files outside the original allowed_paths whitelist. Official validator verdict remains unset and completed_by remains null.
lifecycle.validation_boundary: KERNEL_BUILDER issues no official PASS verdict. Only an Operator-assigned WP Validator or Integration Validator may transition READY_FOR_VALIDATION_V4 to COMPLETED.

scope_waiver.reason: The normal binary had eframe/wgpu integration but no Windows-native wgpu backend and panicked before a usable live window existed. The waived five-line manifest/lock change anchors the already-transitive wgpu 27.0.1 DX12 feature and is the minimum reproducible live-window unblocker.

implementation.summary: Added a Windows-only direct feature anchor for the already-transitive wgpu 27.0.1 package with default-features=false and features=[dx12]; no runtime source logic changed.
implementation.normal_dependency_graph: cargo tree -e normal,features -i wgpu shows one wgpu v27.0.1 with dx12 from handshake-native plus std/WGSL from eframe/egui-wgpu; cargo tree -d reports no wgpu-family duplicate.
implementation.negative_startup_probe: A normal hidden launch with WGPU_BACKEND removed produced responsive=true and published the authenticated binding; the owned process was stopped after proof.

live_printwindow.api: Win32 PrintWindow with PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT against the exact titled Handshake HWND owned by pid 88768
live_printwindow.inspection: The final frame clearly shows the top FILE/EDIT/VIEW/GO/RUN/HELP/EDITORS/OPERATOR menu, STUDIO/LAB/STAGE/INGEST/CKC/MAIN mode tabs, Default Project navigation, Code Symbol editor, Wiki Page editor, Runtime Chat, bottom search/status rails, and readable Retry controls. The disconnected backend state is visible and internally consistent: workspace/document load errors, Runtime Chat EndpointMissing with disabled Send, a local-only alias banner, and Settings persistence retry. Main pane dividers and text remain aligned with no general pane-content collision. Two floating degraded-state panels do obscure underlying content: Propose to Memory overlaps the Wiki header/body region, and Settings persistence overlaps the upper-right Runtime Chat/header region; underlying text is therefore clipped/hidden at those overlay intersections. These are observed live states, not hidden or normalized in the verdict.

headless_deferred.reason: No visible window titled Handshake existed for the headless test pid; the JSON directs the operator/model to rerun from a live Handshake window/GPU host.

build.result: exit 0; dev profile finished; 37 pre-existing future-compatibility warnings

evidence.automation_statement: The live capture and quiet invariants are automatable: resolve the exact titled Handshake HWND for the owned pid, call external PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT), hash the PNG, and compare Win32 foreground/focus/active/capture/cursor/Z-order state before and after. Semantic visual quality still requires opening and inspecting the exact PNG. The authenticated in-process argus.screenshot call deadlocked this live build and UI Automation Invoke foregrounded the app, so neither was accepted as quiet proof; external PrintWindow is the proven automation path.
evidence.user_manual: Existing User Manual coverage is current at manual_content_editors.rs:1042-1050 and 2983-2994: Settings -> Diagnostics, stable target settings.diagnostics.worksurface-inspector.dump, external JSON artifact, screenshot_deferred_headless_gpu meaning, and the prohibition on treating a missing screenshot as visual proof. No manual edit was necessary.
evidence.hbr_int: Flight Recorder NOT_APPLICABLE for the capture itself; internal_diagnostics and Palmistry remain DEFERRED-with-reason while unshipped, per the MT contract.

lifecycle.creation_reason: Created to be the TRUTHFUL NON-PASS OWNER of MT-108 residual item (8), PT-102-B. MT-108 V4 remediation item 6 requires a re-deferred residual to name an owner that REMAINS NON-PASS, and item 7 of the same plan states that a BLOCKED/DEFERRED marker may not close a required pixel row. MT-102 is PASS_V1, so deferring to it would have closed a required pixel row against a passing owner.

scope.summary: Capture the real-GPU worksurface screenshot on a live Handshake window and visually inspect it, closing PT-102-B with pixels rather than a typed deferral.

defect_detail.why_no_cargo_test_can_reach_it: Verified at HEAD 8a77e315. HandshakeApp::capture_worksurface_screenshot_to (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs:12991-13037) delegates to crate::mcp::screenshot::capture_handshake_window(), which is a Win32 PrintWindow capture of a LIVE application window. No cargo test process owns such a window, so no test invocation can produce a real frame.
defect_detail.why_the_existing_test_does_not_prove_it: tests/test_visual_debugger.rs:131-141 accepts EITHER a Deferred OR a Captured outcome. That is correct for a headless CI host but it means the test can never evidence a capture, so a green run says nothing about PT-102-B.
defect_detail.distinct_from_the_wgpu_readback_path: MT-108 current_head_findings finding_2 proves this host CAN materially capture GPU frames with HANDSHAKE_GPU_SCREENSHOT=1 (test_loom_address went 16 passed / 0 failed, EXIT 0, and canvas_loom_chip_screenshot produced real pixels). That is the egui_kittest wgpu READBACK path. PT-102-B is the PrintWindow-on-a-live-window path. The two are different mechanisms and the former does NOT discharge the latter - recorded explicitly so a future implementer does not close this item with the wrong evidence.
defect_detail.host_capability: The host is proven GPU-capable, so this is a live-run and inspection task, not a hardware blocker.

acceptance_criteria: AC-126-1: a real worksurface screenshot is captured from a live Handshake window on a real-GPU host, and the resulting image is OPENED and DESCRIBED - not merely produced. Record the artifact path and its sha256.

AC-126-2: the capture must NOT foreground the app, steal focus, hijack keyboard input, or move the OS cursor, per HBR-QUIET and CX-503D1. PrintWindow on a non-foreground window is the sanctioned mechanism; state how quiet operation was verified.

AC-126-3: the inspection describes what is actually visible - readable controls, no overlap or clipping, correct active/error/disabled states - rather than asserting the file is non-empty. A non-zero byte count is not visual proof.
AC-126-4: the headless path still emits its typed DEFERRED marker and still passes on a host without a window, so CI is not broken by this MT.

AC-126-5: record whether any automated assertion is possible at all on this path. If it genuinely cannot be automated, say so as a typed statement so the next capstone does not re-litigate it from scratch.
proof_targets: PT-126-1: the captured artifact path, its sha256, and a written description of the inspected frame.
PT-126-2: evidence of quiet operation - no foregrounding, no focus or Z-order change during capture.
PT-126-3: the headless deferred-marker path re-run and still green.
scope.risk_if_missed: MT-108 AC-108-1 cannot honestly close: a required pixel row would be closed by a typed deferral against a PASS_V1 owner, which the V4 verdict explicitly forbids.

gui_obligation.requirement: A real captured frame, opened and described. This MT exists precisely because a marker is not a picture.

user_manual_obligation.requirement: Document how an operator or model captures a worksurface screenshot, and what the typed DEFERRED marker means when no GPU window is available.

hbr_obligations.VIS: HBR-VIS: a required pixel row may not be closed by a typed DEFERRED. This MT is the row.
hbr_obligations.QUIET: HBR-QUIET-001: capture must not change foreground window or Z-order.
hbr_obligations.INT: HBR-INT-009: Flight Recorder NOT_APPLICABLE for the capture itself; internal_diagnostics and Palmistry DEFERRED-with-reason while unshipped per CX-981-005.
